$about: 2026-08-06, decisions round: the eight open failures in the `decisions` area - the ADR/BDR machinery, the idea path, and the routing that decides whether a change is a record or a spec update - re-run against the current tree before anything was changed, on the rule that a finding is open only while it still reproduces. Seven reproduced whole. One (DEC-07) reproduced in half: its routing defect is live, and the capability-map half of its 2026-08-04 evidence was already closed by a commit that landed after that round, which is recorded here rather than left implied. Three cases (DEC-03, DEC-12, DEC-13) are anchored to a real repository whose shape was assessed in an earlier round; this round re-ran the standard's half of each - the greps and reads the case's own procedure names - and did not re-assess the target repository, which each evidence field says explicitly.

observations.evidence: Reproduced against the current tree before anything changed, by the case's own procedure. `skills/align-to-standards/onboard.md` step 4 offered exactly one method (enumerate what the code embodies and draft retroactive ADRs) and exactly one destination for material the user hands over: `docs/discovery/<topic>/`, read as "a claim about the code, never as the record itself", with three outcomes - agrees, silent, disagrees - all three ending in a record reconstructed here. `grep -rin 'rfc|upstream|existing decision process|defer' skills/align-to-standards/` returned nothing resembling a defer-to-upstream mode: the only `rfcs/` mention (SKILL.md:157) is in the intake's list of places legacy material might be collected from, which is the opposite framing - it treats an RFC folder as a pile to be filed, not as a process still running. Fixed by adding that mode: a live, formal decision process wired into the merge gate is pointed at rather than re-litigated, and R5 is met by a pointer record in `docs/decision-records/` whose Decision paragraph states the decision in the present tense with the upstream document linked as the authority for context and options. Nothing is copied or paraphrased (a paraphrase drifts from what it summarises), only the decisions this repo's specs and rules will cite get a record, the existing process stays how new decisions are made, and an existing in-repo record layout is mapped rather than migrated - with a manifest `exception` where a required entry is met a different way. What is NOT claimed: rust-lang/rust was not re-assessed this round. The target's shape - RFCs plus MCPs, live and wired into the merge gate - is carried from the 2026-08-03 observation; what was re-run here is the standard's half, which is what the case's procedure names.

Reproduced by the case's own procedure, unchanged from the 2026-08-04 finding: `grep -rn 'idea-write' standard/.claude/skills/` returned two lines, both idea-write's own (`SKILL.md:2` front-matter name, `SKILL.md:6` heading). adr-write's and bdr-write's refusal bullets pointed at `docs/ideas/` - a folder an agent writes to directly - while idea-write's own opening claims both skills "point here instead". Fixed: both refusal bullets now name the skill and say what a hand-written file loses, and the loss is specific rather than rhetorical - idea-write owns `docs/ideas/_template.md`, the rule that an idea serving no persona is parked rather than filed (ADR-006), and the graduation contract that flips the doc to `graduated` with links to what it became. The same grep now returns four lines: idea-write's two, plus `adr-write/SKILL.md:73` and `bdr-write/SKILL.md:74`. Not extended to discovery-digest or add-to-backlog: the case's `given` is the two skills that make the claim, and widening a fix past the defect is how a rule stops biting.

Half of the 2026-08-04 evidence reproduces and half does not, and both halves are recorded. STILL LIVE: idea-write's `-> approved` bullet handed the spec half to `spec-specify` unconditionally ("a behavioral or buildable spec for what it changes (`spec-specify`)"), and spec-specify's directory resolution guarded only an exact name match - "If `specs/<short-name>/` already exists, this is the same capability". The short name is derived from the words of the request, and an idea's slug names the idea, so an approved idea changing an existing capability's approval logic misses that guard by construction and mints a sibling directory. ALREADY CLOSED: the second half of the 2026-08-04 evidence - "R11's capability-map entry was never created by either skill" - does not reproduce. `git log -S` locates the closing change as commit 1ed3d3c (2026-08-04 20:18, "author the capability map on the greenfield path, and keep it current"), which added spec-specify's "Register the capability in `specs/capability-map.json`" step; that step is in the tree today, so the finding is narrower than the round that logged it. Fixed for the live half in two places: idea-write routes the spec half through `spec-impact` and names `spec-update` for an existing owner, and spec-specify carries the same correction at the point the directory is minted - a name miss is explicitly not evidence that a capability is new, and a minted directory is named after the capability, never after the request or the idea.

Reproduced by reading `standard/.claude/skills/spec-impact/SKILL.md` step 3 against the case: the ripple search listed exactly three bullets - other capability specs, ADRs, and code/files - and the Output block listed four lines, none naming any artifact outside `specs/`, the records and the code. So the four artifacts the 2026-08-04 round falsified simultaneously (a runbook, a persona description, a PRODUCT line and a backlog row) were not merely missed by an agent; nothing in the skill asks about them. Fixed by a fifth bullet requiring a verdict per artifact - the sentence this change falsifies, or untouched - across `docs/runbooks/`, `docs/personas.md`, `docs/PRODUCT.md`, `docs/analytics.md` and the backlog, plus the matching Output line so a missing verdict is visible rather than absent. Kept from degenerating into "read everything": the search keys on the capability's own terms, because a sentence that contradicts the change is a sentence that names the thing being changed. What is NOT claimed: this is the skill's text, re-read against the case, not a re-run of the fixture - the fixture that produced the original four contradictions is not in this checkout.

Reproduced verbatim against the three shipped files. `spec-update/SKILL.md:17-18` - "If any of them has `Status: retired`, stop before editing it". `spec-reconcile/SKILL.md:33-36` - a cross-spec contradiction "is a finding - resolve it in this change if it belongs here", under a document whose closing line is "No knowingly-contradicting spec merges (rule 8: no silent drift)". `spec-impact/SKILL.md:19` - "Check the primary spec's `Status` first", with the ripple search below it carrying no status check at all. Three rules, three directions, and the one that would detect the case scoped so it cannot: undetectable, then simultaneously forbidden and required. Not resolved by rewording two of them, because choosing which one gives way is a decision: ADR-036 records it, with the three rejected alternatives - freeze the file and record the contradiction elsewhere (leaves false text standing as current truth, against R4), reopen the capability by side effect (undoes a recorded retirement without a decision), delete the stale section (destroys what retirement keeps the file for). The decision is that `retired` freezes behaviour, not truth: no new behaviour ever, and a correction whenever a change makes a statement false, in that change's own pull request, bounded to what the capability did plus what superseded it. The record claims no guard and says why - no check can distinguish a correction from an extension by reading a diff, and one gating on size or section is satisfied by splitting the change. The three skills, the spec template's retirement note and `specs/spec-engine/spec.md` now state the one path.

Reproduced by running the real script, not by reading it. A copy of the shipped tree plus a `.standards-version`, carrying `docs/decision-records/adr/ADR-001-use-postgres.md` built from the shipped template with Status, Date and Tags substituted and `| **Author** | {{AUTHOR}} |` left exactly as the template ships it: `node scripts/self-verify.mjs` raised five `still carries template placeholders` warnings (AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/PRODUCT.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/backlog.md) and none of them named the record. The only line in the whole run mentioning the record came from a different check entirely - the index guard noting it has no README row. The cause is not the token's syntax: `{{...}}` is already one of the three shapes the pattern matches (`{{NORTH_STAR}}` in PRODUCT). It is the scanned set, a fixed list of eight entry documents that never included `docs/decision-records/`. Fixed by reaching the records through the record filename pattern rather than a directory, so both shipped layouts work and `_template.md` and the stream READMEs are excluded by construction. Four cases in `tools/self-verify-fill-test.mjs` hold both directions, and they were checked adversarially rather than assumed: with the record enumeration short-circuited to an empty list, exactly the two positive cases fail (`expected [["ADR-001-use-postgres.md",true]]` and `expected [["BDR-004-target-personas.md",true]]`) while the negative ones still pass - so they measure the fix, and the negative pair is what would catch a scan widened until it warns on the templates it came from. adr-write and bdr-write now also say to fill the row with a person, which is the half no check can do: catching a persona name written there is judgment, not pattern-matching.

Reproduced by the case's own procedure against the current tree: `grep -ri 'cran\|external release gate\|gatekeep' docs/method/checklist.md docs/method/changelog-process.md standard/SPEC.md` returned no output at all. The Delivery axis's own row still read "the **maintainer cuts releases**", which is the assumption the case names - it presumes the repo owns the gate. Fixed by adding the fork rather than rewriting the assumption, since for most repos the assumption holds and is the paved road: a new Delivery row for a release gate owned by a third party, covering a registry that reviews submissions or re-checks and archives already-published versions on its own schedule, an app store review, a distribution's packaging process, and an internal release board. The paved road asks for the three things that are actually decidable - name the gate and what it can do to a published release, decide who watches it and how the repo learns, decide the response (fix window, who may cut an out-of-cycle release, what happens when the deadline passes) - and keeps "does not apply" as the expected answer, which the catalog already treats as an answer worth a line. What is NOT claimed: Rdatatable/data.table was not re-assessed this round, and no new claim is made about CRAN's mechanics beyond the behaviour the 2026-08-06 wave-6 observation recorded.

Reproduced against the current tree. `skills/align-to-standards/onboard.md` step 4 opens "The code embodies decisions" and enumerates from what the code shows - the method assumes a fingerprint in the tree - and `grep -rin 'founding\|fork\|licen' skills/align-to-standards/onboard.md` returned nothing, so no shape of the case was addressed anywhere in the phase. The nearest available destination, `docs/discovery/`, is non-normative by ADR-024, which the shipped skills restate in their own words (`spec-specify`: "A dossier is never normative"), so it cannot hold the record either - both halves of the case's `then` held. Fixed by naming the shape and giving it a route: a founding or identity decision is recognised by two symptoms an agent can check (it predates the first commit, or its rejected options are alternative projects rather than alternative implementations), it is written as a record from stated rationale rather than reconstructed from the tree, it cites where each part came from and says plainly that the source is outside the repo, and it is the one record in this pass an agent may not quietly assert - unconfirmed by a human it is drafted `Proposed` with the open question named, because nothing in the tree lets the next reader check it. What is NOT claimed: opentofu/opentofu was not re-cloned or re-assessed this round; the target's shape is carried from the 2026-08-06 wave-6 observation, and what was re-run here is the standard's half, which is what the case's procedure names.
